prompt:
A RailOps Data & Booking Operations system with main features including offline schedule aggregation, ticket order administration, contractor credential handling, and quality-controlled data ingestion for a regional rail operator. The Yew-based web UI provides two primary workspaces: a public-facing kiosk mode for station staff to search service content and assist customers, and an internal operations console for authenticated users. Riders’ service information is presented through on-site full-text search with fuzzy matching and relevance weighting, plus multi-condition filters such as departure time window, city, category (fares, delays, baggage), and tags; the UI also auto-publishes archive pages by day and route and shows “related content” based on tag overlap and similarity rules. Operations Admins and Customer Service Agents use the console to monitor train schedules and seat inventory by departure, search orders by passenger name/partial phone, and perform manual handling actions such as rebooking, canceling, or fee overrides with a required reason note. Business rules are configurable by authorized staff: an order hold expires after 15 minutes if not confirmed, refunds requested more than 24 hours before departure return the fare minus a $5.00 processing fee, refunds within 2–24 hours return 50%, and refunds under 2 hours are blocked except for “service disruption” cases. A staffing view supports intelligent matching for temporary conductors/drivers by region, availability window, required tags, and historical quality ratings, with two-way subscriptions so dispatchers can follow critical shifts and contractors can follow preferred routes; UI feedback must show match scores and the top three reasons a candidate was ranked.

The backend uses Actix-web to expose a decoupled REST-style API consumed by the Yew frontend over local TLS, with PostgreSQL as the system of record for orders, schedules, inventory snapshots, content pages, matching profiles, and immutable audit logs. A configurable multi-source collection engine runs on-prem and ingests from preloaded local “site” packages or internal mirrors (no internet dependency), supporting task definitions by source, city, keyword, and pagination rules, incremental updates, resumable crawling after interruption, per-task rate limits (default 2 requests/second equivalent per source), and global concurrency caps (default 10 workers). Data cleansing enforces deduplication by URL fingerprint plus content similarity (quarantine if similarity ≥ 0.92), detects missing critical fields and anomalies (e.g., negative fare, departure in the past), assigns a quality score (completeness 50%, accuracy 30%, timeliness 20%) and blocks publishing below 85/100, while writing traceable cleansing logs and enabling sampling-based review (default 2% of records per batch) with replay of the exact transformation steps. Privacy and security require local username/password login only (minimum 12 characters, lockout for 15 minutes after 5 failures), role-based access with tiered permissions, signed API requests between UI and server, server-side rate limiting (e.g., 60 requests/minute per session), and session expiration after 30 minutes idle. Sensitive data is minimized and masked in displays (phone shown as (XXX) XXX-1234), encrypted in transit and at rest (AES-256), and supports deletion workflows (PII purged 30 days after trip completion upon request) while retaining audit trails for 7 years. Contract and credential document management stores PDFs/JPEG/PNG up to 10 MB, validates file type and fingerprint, tracks expiration dates entered by staff, applies view-time watermarks (viewer + timestamp), and logs every review/approval action with tamper-evident audit entries; e-signing is supported via an internal capture flow (typed name and date, plus optional drawn signature) without relying on any external service.
